scenarioStory.history: Maintenance electrician contacted an overhead high-voltage line while working on a catwalk, was thrown approximately 8 feet by the resulting muscle contraction, and found down by coworkers. Power was confirmed shut off at the breaker before bystanders began CPR.
scenarioStory.course: Initial Contact: Crew arrives to find a 37-year-old male in cardiac arrest following high-voltage electrical contact. Bystander CPR is in progress; coworkers confirm the power source has been shut off and the scene is safe to approach. → CPR and defibrillation initiated: Crew confirms pulseless VF, resumes high-quality chest compressions, and delivers manufacturer-recommended defibrillation while establishing IV/IO access for epinephrine. → ROSC achieved, burns addressed: The patient regains return of spontaneous circulation with an organized sinus tachycardia. Crew now identifies and dresses the entry/exit burn wounds, assesses for associated trauma from the fall, and prepares for transport to a burn/trauma-capable center.

patientInformation.patientCondition: Cardiac arrest following high-voltage electrical contact

scenarioEvents.name: Initial Contact
scenarioEvents.description: Crew arrives to find a 37-year-old male in cardiac arrest following high-voltage electrical contact. Bystander CPR is in progress; coworkers confirm the power source has been shut off and the scene is safe to approach.
relatedChecklist: Identify and treat dysrhythmia/arrest from electrical contact per Cardiac Arrest protocol
Resume high-quality chest compressions immediately, minimize interruptions
Defibrillate coarse VF at maximum biphasic setting per manufacturer (e.g., 200 J)
Apply continuous cardiac monitor and obtain 12-lead EKG as soon as feasible
Epinephrine 1 mg IV/IO during the first or second compression cycle

scenarioEvents.name: CPR and defibrillation initiated
scenarioEvents.description: Crew confirms pulseless VF, resumes high-quality chest compressions, and delivers manufacturer-recommended defibrillation while establishing IV/IO access for epinephrine.
relatedChecklist: Treat per Post-ROSC Care Guideline: titrate oxygen to SpO2 94-98%, avoid hyperventilation
Identify and dress entry (right palm) and exit (left heel) burn wounds with dry dressings
Assess for compartment syndrome from extremity tissue damage
Apply spinal motion restriction given the fall from the contact point
Transport to a burn center capable of managing electrical injury; report voltage/AC-DC characteristics to receiving facility

scenarioEvents.name: ROSC achieved, burns addressed
scenarioEvents.description: The patient regains return of spontaneous circulation with an organized sinus tachycardia. Crew now identifies and dresses the entry/exit burn wounds, assesses for associated trauma from the fall, and prepares for transport to a burn/trauma-capable center.

scenarioEvents.name: Defibrillation delayed for burn assessment
scenarioEvents.description: Crew becomes fixated on examining the dramatic entry/exit burn wounds and delays defibrillation, allowing VF to persist. Prolonged downtime without definitive rhythm treatment lowers the chance of a good outcome.
relatedChecklist: Recognize refractory VF from delayed defibrillation; resume compressions and shock immediately
Amiodarone 300 mg IV/IO for refractory VF after continued shocks
